2.reason: the reviewer's own run at head 902372b946 shows the repaired test and the node's three tests passing (logs/head-single-test.log)

findings.text: _held_records_signature signs the merged ledger, git's worktree registry and the live directory, but the derivation it guards (obligations.py:1849) also tests path.is_dir() on every registered worktree, and no signed input moves when a tree directory is removed without a registry update, so a held record can be served stale for the cache's whole life because the cache carries no expiry.

The 118.745 s and 75.761 s figures are quoted as the measured live cost, but the log behind them (logs/live-payload-timing.log) ends with NameError: name '_trim' is not defined before it reaches its payload-equality check, stamps EXIT=0 anyway, and was taken at d966cc8d2c rather than at the landed head 902372b946.

The after_suite arm is recorded at revision 258296b3c9 and carries an added failure (test_a_delivered_pointer_costs_one_head_resolution) that the worker repaired in 39e28645b0 with no arm re-recorded at head; an independent run of that test plus this node's three tests at 902372b946 passes (4 passed, logs/head-single-test.log), so the promoted evidence overstates the failure and does not itself show it gone.

_cached is a second thread-safe bounded memo (_CACHE_LOCK, _CACHE_LIMIT, clear-on-full) beside the one reckon/file_memo.py:358 already owns; that owner keys on a single file's stat identity and cannot express this composite key, so the addition duplicates only file_memo's plumbing, but a key-carrying variant of memoized would have kept one memo policy in the repository.
